trust_decision.summary: No runtime trust decision is added or modified anywhere: the published fix only re-declares the GraphQL variables map value type as @Nullable in ten API files, so every path behaves identically before and after; the advisory's unsafe-deserialization property is not addressed by this diff at all, and the tree's only default-typing sink (keyset cursor) is untouched.

landing_point.why: It is the only place in the tree that enables Jackson default typing, and its input is the client-supplied after/before cursor (SubrangeMethodArgumentResolver.java:57-66), so an 'unsafe deserialization' report leads here first.

fix_sites.entry_point: GraphQlRequest.getVariables() - interface implemented by every server request type
DefaultGraphQlRequest(String, String, Map, Map) constructor / getVariables()
DefaultExecutionGraphQlRequest constructor - server-side execution request API
WebGraphQlRequest(URI, HttpHeaders, ..., Map body, ...) - HTTP/WebSocket request body binding
SerializableGraphQlRequest.setVariables - JSON body bound by Jackson from the HTTP/WebSocket request
DefaultClientGraphQlRequest constructor - used by the HTTP/WebSocket transports

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Both live in modules the published library does not ship: the docs sample sits in spring-graphql-docs (moduleProjects lists only spring-graphql and spring-graphql-test, build.gradle:8) and the Jackson 2 fallback only runs when Jackson 3 is absent, so a solver can argue each is 'sample/legacy, not the advisory'.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Keyset cursors must keep round-tripping Date, Calendar, UUID, Number/BigDecimal and java.time values through the JSON type-id form; a deny-all or blanket 'no default typing' fix breaks keyset pagination.

O6_input_shapes: bulk variables map whose values may be null: Map<String, Object> becomes Map<String, @Nullable Object> on GraphQlClient.variables, GraphQlTester.variables and GraphQlRequest.getVariables
single variable value already declared @Nullable (GraphQlClient.RequestSpec.variable, GraphQlTester.Request.variable) - the bulk-map shape is aligned to it

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Jackson 2 fallback mapper for the same cursor decode guards only by base type (allowIfBaseType(Map.class)) instead of an explicit subtype allow-list, so any named subtype is accepted when the declared base type is a Map
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: legacy compatibility path, only selected when Jackson 3 (tools.jackson) is absent, so modern Spring Framework 7 never reaches it
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, adjacent nested class (0 packages)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Public JsonKeysetCursorStrategy(CodecConfigurer) constructor takes the caller's JSON decoder, so the built-in polymorphic-type validation is not applied at all on this construction path
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: caller-supplied codec - the application, not the library, owns mapper configuration; the docs sample uses exactly this constructor at KeysetCursorConfiguration.java:55-59
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file/package; exercised from the docs module

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second cursor codec variant per Jackson generation with its own validator list
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the file already ships two parallel mapper customizers, one per Jackson generation; a maintainer adding support for another Jackson line would copy the structure and can easily copy the older, broader validator

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an application-side @Configuration building its own JsonMapper with default typing and wiring it through the public CodecConfigurer constructor
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: docs samples copy the library configuration and already diverge here (allowIfBaseType instead of the library's subtype allow-list), so a hardened sample or a second sample for another keyset type would be natural

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a parallel CursorStrategy implementation that reuses a caller-provided decoder for a different cursor encoding
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the public CodecConfigurer constructor exists so applications can inject codecs, and CursorStrategy is a public SPI (data/pagination/CursorStrategy.java:31-51) that invites alternative implementations

O10_build.toolchain: Gradle 9.4.1 wrapper with buildSrc conventions, Java 25 toolchain (graphQlJavaVersion = 25.0), multi-release jar targeting Java 21, Kotlin plugin; Spring Framework 7.0.8-SNAPSHOT and graphql-java 25.0 resolved from mavenCentral/repo.spring.io
O10_build.project_tests: JUnit 5 + AssertJ unit tests cover the affected area offline: JsonKeysetCursorStrategyTests, ScrollPositionCursorStrategyTests, Base64CursorEncoderTests; the variables API is covered by GraphQlClientTests and HttpGraphQlTransportIntegrationTests. The full suite also pulls Testcontainers MongoDB/Neo4j and Selenium (spring-graphql/build.gradle:83-85,102-103), but not for these classes.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Declare the variables map values @Nullable (what the published diff does) - a source-only change with no runtime effect - instead of hardening the mapper that decodes untrusted type ids.
